metas.name: Nocturnal Animals
metas.description: An art dealer reads her ex-husband's brutal novel, and the story bleeds into her own guilt. Tom Ford controls every frame, the menace keeps rising and the revenge ending is cold.

metas.name: Elle
metas.description: Verhoeven's thriller about a game-company boss who responds to an assault in ways no one expects. Darkly funny, deeply uncomfortable and completely controlled.

metas.name: A Simple Plan
metas.description: Three ordinary men find a crashed plane full of cash, and keeping it turns decent people into killers one reasonable step at a time. Sam Raimi's most precise film.

metas.name: Zodiac
metas.description: Fincher's obsessive serial-killer procedural, where the search eats the lives of the men running it. The basement scene is one of the most frightening sequences of its decade.

metas.name: Coherence
metas.description: At a dinner party on the night a comet passes, the friends start meeting other versions of themselves, and trust falls apart one door-knock at a time. It's a tight, low-budget puzzle about doubles, and the last twist keeps paying off long after it ends.

metas.name: Primal Fear
metas.description: A slick defense lawyer takes on an altar boy accused of murdering an archbishop, and the case turns on a performance that may or may not be real. It builds steadily to one of the great last-minute reversals.

metas.name: Infinity Pool
metas.description: On a resort island, rich tourists can pay to have a double executed for their crimes, and a struggling writer gets pulled into the game. Brandon Cronenberg makes it a cruel, hypnotic film about identity and impunity.

metas.name: Side Effects
metas.description: A young woman on a new antidepressant commits a violent act, and her psychiatrist's life comes apart as he digs into what really happened. Soderbergh's cool, precise thriller keeps flipping who is performing for whom.

metas.name: Stoker
metas.description: After her father dies, a strange teenager's charming uncle moves in, and she finds out how much they have in common. Park Chan-wook's English-language debut is precise, perverse and beautifully controlled.
